result.summary:
The audit's BLOCKING call is correct and survives: "Both sit at the same table." is an added claim in no WAS line, it fails 42a on its own test, and it must be cut before anything lands. Its mechanical sweep is also correct — I re-ran it over the delivered text with the WAS lines stripped and got zero hits for em dash, exclamation, semicolon, contraction, first person, will/shall, bare priest/mayor/singular elder, and every struck archaism including "drinking house", "pedlar" and "granary"; the only digit hits are metadata lines, not prose.

But the audit is INCOMPLETE in the one way that matters to the freeze: IT LEFT A CHANGED LINE UNEXAMINED. The file marks seven CHANGED faces at lines 12, 24, 31, 41, 44, 47 and 54. The return analyses six. Variant 3 face 6 [muster] — line 54, "The muster's account is that what reaches it first is the shouting, and that the shouting is enough to go on." re-cut to "The muster reckons what reaches it first is the shouting, and the shouting is enough to go on." — is named nowhere in the return, not in the findings, not in the untouched list, not in leastSure. An unexamined changed line is an unrefuted line, and it carries a real attribution defect (finding 1 below). The audit's own facesChanged count of 7 is right; its coverage is 6.

THE MOVED CLAIM IT PASSED OVER IS THE ONE IT AFFIRMATIVELY CLEARED. At variant 1 face 4 the audit records "No defect ... The claim is identical" and calls it "the model the other five untouched 42d failures should have been cut to". The claim is not identical. "the same words go over the house" names no agent; "they speak the same words over the house" makes the ground-keepers the officiants. A game master reading the new line places them at the graveside performing the rite — a fact the old line did not license, and one the standing refutation never tested. This matters twice over, because the audit flagged exactly this class as a moved claim one finding earlier at variant 3 face 2 ("what is given here" to "what they give here") and then blessed it here. Its leastSure #3 asks for the principled line between these; here it is, and it settles all four pronoun insertions: inserting the speaker as the PATIENT of an act the settlement's people still perform keeps the subject, the act and the habitual frame, so V2F1 "lends him a thing" is lawful 42d; REPLACING a generic or agentless SUBJECT with the speaker shrinks the claim, so V3F1 "a visitor here learns" to "he learns", V3F2, and V1F4 are all narrowings that must be collected for re-refutation. The audit collected two of the three and cleared the third.

ITS REMEDIES ARE LESS SAFE THAN ITS DIAGNOSES. The shape finding is right that 20 of 20 faces are role-says-a-fact and right that the freeze forecloses most alternatives, but its three "free conversions" each strip the reporting verb and turn a source's self-report into an engine-asserted fact; the brief licenses the speakerless shape only "where the engine itself holds it", which is the clause the finding does not quote. Its V2F4 fix keeps "the men who take the work" — the very class its own finding says may be invented and off-card. And across the twelve untouched lines, several proposed fixes are themselves 42b sharpenings that pick a reading (the variant 1 spine's "a running account of which house owes which", variant 2 face 3's "they let a stranger in on what is in his pack"), yet only one of them, V2F6, carries the re-refute caveat. Every one of those needs the caveat or none do.

Two smaller corrections. The pair-1 claim is overstated: the narrowed elders line still collides head on with the tavern half over the elders' own giving, because the tavern half covers all giving — the disagreement narrows, it does not stop. And the headline arithmetic does not close: 23 lines minus 12 untouched failures leaves 11, and the audit's own findings fail three more changed lines (V3F3, V3F2, V2F4) with a fourth never assessed, which gives 8 passing, not the 10 reported. The direction of the gain is real; the number should not be quoted.

The second "that" was dropped, which lets the second clause escape the attribution: "The muster reckons X, and the shouting is enough to go on" can be parsed as a claim the muster makes or as the narrator's own assertion coordinated with the whole main clause. Under the WAS line a game master knows only that the muster THINKS shouting is enough, and can play the muster as complacent and wrong; under one available reading of the NOW line the shouting really is enough, which is an engine-held fact about the settlement's readiness and not a muster opinion. That is a moved claim on the reading, and a 42b breach in any case, because two readings now fit the sentence. Separately "The muster's account is that" became "The muster reckons", which downgrades a report the muster has given into an opinion it holds; on a pool whose machinery turns on witnesses and what is on the record, those are different facts. Restoring the parallel "that" fixes both the ambiguity and the escape while keeping the shorter verb the implementer wanted.

This one should be struck from the remainder list rather than cut. The audit calls "and nobody there says why" a trailing clause that adds no fact and is the writer pointing at significance. result.summary: The audit is sound where it looked and missed the thing it was most pointed at. I re-ran the mechanical sweep myself and it is CONFIRMED clean on every bar — no em dash, semicolon, exclamation, digit in prose, will/shall, first person, bare role or brace, and all five apostrophes are possessives; granary survives only in the pool's title line and factor only in two WAS lines, so the 42c cure did land in both places. Both BLOCKING calls survive independent checking: V2 F7 really does convert a habitual into a one-off past event, and V3 F1's 'is sent him instead' really does swap an unnamed person for the speaking priest while widening 'the house' to 'a house at all'. One finding is overturned: the 42b pronoun collision at V1 F8 does not stand, because only one antecedent for 'it' is semantically available; the sharpening the auditor filed on the same face is correct and stays. The material miss is a dropped attribution on a sourced face — V2 FACE 4 [market], where the cut split a sentence and left the second fact self-standing, turning a stallholder's claim into the engine's own assertion. The auditor caught exactly this pattern on the V2 SPINE, rated it a NOTE because a spine is unsourced, and then blessed the identical split on a sourced face as 'surviving the 42a test'. The test it needed was not 42a but the frame: the two lines that were already two sentences at HEAD both have anaphorically bound second sentences ('neither', 'that good') that cannot be read as narration, and this new one has no back-reference at all. Three further misses: V1 F1 is an undeclared 42b sharpening that the auditor filed as a chair question with no collection row, so on the keep branch it ships unrefuted; V3 F3's 'has ever bothered', which the auditor called good and worth keeping, imports a motive (indifference) and a perfect tense the old line did not carry; and the five attribution-verb swaps change the claim's standing from asserted to believed, an argument the auditor made for 'has it that' alone and did not carry to the other four. Finally the credit is inflated. There were seven 'and that' edits, not six, and I applied the 42a delete test to all seven — every surviving clause carries a fact, so ruling 42 was never engaged by any of them and those edits are cosmetic. The 13-of-25 to 20-of-25 pass count is not reconstructible on that basis and should be re-derived before the chair reads it. Disposition unchanged in kind but not in weight: still LANDABLE_AFTER_FIXES, now with three BLOCKING repairs rather than two, and with V1 F1, V1 F8 and V3 F3 all needing collection for the refuter.

overturnedFindings.why: The finding does not survive as an actionable defect of this cut, on three grounds. First, its only concrete remedy breaks the freeze the audit exists to enforce. The proposed variant 3 face 1 rewrite, "A drover found a bed for himself and shelter for his beasts without anyone going out of their way", deletes the town as the agent of provision; HEAD and NOW both read "the town found him a bed and his beasts shelter", and in an Economic Survival pool whether the town provided or the drover located provision is the entire content of the face. The proposed variant 1 face 1 rewrite converts "A travelling trader SAYS the trestle ... had been mended" into "A travelling trader FOUND the trestle ... mended", which promotes a stranger's testimony into a narrated event the engine vouches for — the same evidential move, in the hardening direction, that the auditor rightly faulted at variant 1 face 9. Second, the freeze forbids deleting a speaker, which makes the bare DOES shape and the bare-fact-with-no-speaker shape structurally unavailable to a line edit; faulting a line editor for not using shapes the freeze prohibits is not a defect of the cut. Third, the absolute is not true of the pool: variant 2 face 9 ("Nothing about the town's own paying has ever been brought as a quarrel"), variant 3 face 6 ("nobody from the hall has come to the trades for a figure") and variant 3 face 9 ("the purse has never come before them") all carry the NOBODY-HAS-DONE shape the brief lists as lawful, and variant 1 face 10, variant 2 face 6 and variant 2 face 9 front the fact with mid- or end-sentence attribution rather than opening with the role. The observation is worth keeping for the chair in one line — shape variety is a draft-time property and cannot be added by a line edit without moving claims — but it is not a fix this implementer owed and not one that can be safely applied now. The auditor also contradicts itself here: its own variant 1 face 10 fix converts a fact-fronted line into precisely the "role says fact" shape it calls monotonous.

overturnedFindings.faceOrSpine: POOL — the SHAPE_MONOTONY sub-claim that eight edits "went the wrong way" by flattening "X's account is that" into "X says"
overturnedFindings.why: This is wrong on the owner's own evidence. None of the six worked lines contains a nominal attribution frame; every one is a plain verb of saying or a plain action verb — "A clerk at the town hall says", "A priest says", "At the tavern they say", "A traveller found", "Local families repair the walls". Ruling 42c is a rule about plain modern words and 42 is CLEAR BEFORE CRAFTED; "The sexton's word is that", "By the account of those who hold the way through" and "The guilds' own reckoning is that" are the crafted register both rulings withdraw. The auditor's stated ground is that the flattening spends surface variety, but surface variety in attribution frames is not a standard anywhere in the brief, and preserving a mannered frame to keep it would set 42c against itself. The flattening is the cut doing what it was asked to do. Two of these conversions do deserve findings, and they deserve them for a different reason — the reporting verb changed evidential force at variant 1 face 9 ("reckon") and at variant 2 face 3 ("holds"), the first of which the auditor caught and the second of which it missed. The count is also understated: I make it roughly a dozen such conversions, not eight, which cuts against the characterisation rather than for it.

result.summary: The audit's spine stands and its headline is right: the claim freeze did not hold, the named 42c sweep is genuinely complete, both disagreement pairs still disagree, and the variant 3 face 5 speaker swap is a real blocking defect. I re-verified the mechanical bars independently against the live text and found no breach — no em dash, exclamation, digit, semicolon, first person, will or shall, and the four apostrophes are all possessives, not contractions. What the audit missed is a second moved claim inside its own blocking finding: variant 3 face 5 also narrowed \"the people who would be wanted first\" to \"the men\", an added fact about who the town calls, and the auditor's proposed fix carries that narrowing forward, so applying its fix as written leaves the pool with a moved claim after the block is nominally cured. It also missed the evidential move at variant 2 face 3, where the hall's own on-the-record answer became one clerk's opinion — the same family as the \"reckon\" note it did raise, but two steps instead of one and against the hall's own card — and it described the resulting opener collision as two-way when grep shows \"A clerk in the hall\" now opens the hall face in all three variants. Two of the audit's own proposed fixes are unsafe and must not be applied: the variant 1 spine fix flips \"meets it short\" to \"meets it with nothing to spare\", which moves the pool's thesis line from shortfall to sufficiency in an ADEQUATE-band pool, and the FOUND rewrites offered under SHAPE_MONOTONY delete the town as the agent of provision at variant 3 face 1 and promote a stranger's testimony into narrated engine fact at variant 1 face 1. SHAPE_MONOTONY itself does not survive as an actionable finding, because the freeze forbids deleting a speaker and therefore forbids the bare shapes it asks for, because several faces already carry the lawful NOBODY-HAS-DONE shape it says are absent, and because its only remedy breaks the freeze; and its sub-claim that flattening \"X's account is that\" into \"X says\" went the wrong way is refuted by the owner's six worked lines, none of which uses a nominal attribution frame. Finally the refutation-debt list is short by two: the audit collected one sharpening and then proposed two more of its own. Net: the cut is landable after fixes, but the audit's fix list must be corrected before anyone applies it, and the safest cures for the three real claim moves are all reverts.

The mechanical sweep re-runs clean under my own greps and I confirm every part of it: no em dash, semicolon, exclamation, digit on any prose line, contraction (all five apostrophes in the file are possessives — household's, stranger's, somebody's), first person, will/shall, literal settlement token, bare priest/mayor/singular elder, or struck archaism in either column; the register is intact at 10/9/8 faces, 27 faces plus 3 spines, 9 changed and 18 unchanged. The auditor's BLOCKING finding at V2 FACE 1 survives and I do not disturb it, but its routing is mislabelled: "What is put into a hand here is goods and not coin" was a definite generic claim, not a two-reading vague one, so the edit is a CLAIM_MOVED that simply reverts, not a 42b sharpening to be queued for re-refutation. Its proposed fix reverts correctly, so the text lands the same either way, but it must not go to the refuter as new work.

What the audit missed is the thing it affirmatively blessed. Six of the nine edits are comma-to-period splits, and the auditor cleared all six on the 42a test alone ("already lawful under 42a and the split buys legibility, not a standard crossing") without once asking what a period does to the attribution's scope. In every one of the six, the trailing and-clause was a coordinate inside the speaker's complement — the pool proves its own house pattern at V3 FACE 5, "The muster says the ground it would gather on is somebody's own field, and that somebody would bear the trampling of the crop," where the explicit "and that" marks the trailing clause as part of the said thing. After the split, "The purse comes after the roof, the water and the grain," "Not one of the doors opens," "No one has walked them past its shelves" and the rest stand as free narration. A fact a watchman is quoted holding and a fact the engine holds are not the same fact: the first needs only to be sayable, the second must be true of the card, and the standing refutation covered the first. The brief's claim freeze names this in terms: NO SPEAKER MAY BE DELETED AND NO ATTRIBUTION DROPPED. I grade the family SHOULD_FIX rather than BLOCKING only because the owner's own worked model ("A priest says the sick house takes anyone who comes. The grain store turns away anyone without an order.") shows an unattributed second sentence still read as continuing testimony, and four unchanged faces in this pool already use the shape — so the attribution is made ambiguous rather than certainly destroyed. The cure is one clause per face and costs nothing.

Two further items. V1 FACE 6 is worse than the auditor's NOTE: moving "the same backs" out of the reported clause and into the subject of "say" puts the contested half of pair 1 into the narration as a presupposition, so the pool now takes its own side in its own disagreement pair. And on V1 FACE 3 the auditor's leastSure entry is right and its grading is wrong — "a visitor is handed the unmarked pail" is a standing arrangement and "he was handed the unmarked one" is one past event; the arrangement is the fact, the anecdote is not, and the definite article carries an implicature, not the claim. That is a claim move on the freeze's literal terms and belongs at SHOULD_FIX, not NOTE. Its fix is already written and correct.

Two of the auditor's five findings do not survive as filed: the 42a breach at V3 FACE 8 (the rule's own test returns PASS, and the fix deletes an attributed claim) and the instance evidence under SHAPE_MONOTONY (ten fact-first lines survive the cut, not one). I also note without filing that three of the auditor's advisory fixes for untouched faces introduce facts the originals do not carry — the V2 spine gains "Nothing worse than that has been asked of them," a historical claim where the original had a belief, and V3 FACE 3 gains "they have never known a household fail," a claim about the elders' own experience. Only its V3 FACE 7 fix is declared as needing refutation. Those two should be declared the same way or dropped.

missedFindings.faceOrSpine: V1 FACE 7 [garrison], V1 FACE 8 [watch], V2 FACE 3 [tavern], V2 FACE 8 [watch], V3 FACE 8 [garrison] (V2 FACE 5 filed separately)
missedFindings.was: One of the watch says the round is walked before anything is settled, and the purse comes after the roof, the water and the grain.
missedFindings.now: One of the watch says the round is walked before anything is settled. The purse comes after the roof, the water and the grain.
missedFindings.why: The auditor cleared all five of these splits on the 42a test and never ran the attribution test the claim freeze requires. In each WAS line the trailing and-clause is a coordinate inside the speaker's complement: the pool marks this pattern explicitly at V3 FACE 5, 'The muster says the ground it would gather on is somebody's own field, AND THAT somebody would bear the trampling of the crop,' where 'and that' can only be a second complement of 'says'. After the period, 'The purse comes after the roof, the water and the grain' is free narration. The same applies to 'No one has walked them past its shelves' (V1 F7, where 'by their own account' is a mid-sentence parenthetical that cannot scope forward across a full stop), 'The ones asked first sit quiet over their cups' (V2 F3), 'The round ends where it starts, at the water' (V2 F8) and 'The people here ask them straight out to put a shoulder to a load' (V3 F8). A fact attributed to a speaker need only be sayable; a fact in the engine's own voice must be true of the card. The refutation these faces carry was run against attributed speech, so the escalation is not covered. The brief states the bar without qualification: NO SPEAKER MAY BE DELETED AND NO ATTRIBUTION DROPPED. Held at SHOULD_FIX rather than BLOCKING because the owner's own model line ('A priest says the sick house takes anyone who comes. The grain store turns away anyone without an order.') and four unchanged faces in this pool show a period does not always expel a sentence from the speaker's mouth; the attribution is made ambiguous rather than certainly destroyed, and ambiguity about who holds a fact is itself the defect.
missedFindings.proposedFix: Carry the attribution into the second sentence rather than reverting the comma, which keeps the legibility the split bought and costs one clause: 'One of the watch says the round is walked before anything is settled. The purse, he says, comes after the roof, the water and the grain.' The same cure applies to the other four faces.

missedFindings.was: The bar coming down is heard at the far doors, by the account of those who hold the way through, and not one of the doors opens.
missedFindings.now: Those who hold the way through say the bar coming down is heard at the far doors. Not one of the doors opens.
missedFindings.why: This is the sharpest instance in the family and is a relocation, not a re-punctuation, so it is not covered by the ambiguity defence that holds the other five at SHOULD_FIX. In the WAS line the attribution phrase sits BETWEEN the two reported facts and governs both: 'heard at the far doors' and 'not one of the doors opens' are alike 'by the account of those who hold the way through'. The re-cut converted that scope-spanning parenthetical into a leading verb that governs only the first clause, and left the second standing alone. The fact it left standing alone is the pool's strongest community-behaviour claim and an absolute negative: nobody opens a door when the bar comes down. In a WEAK economic-survival pool that is the load-bearing line about whether anyone turns out, and it is now narrator-certified rather than gatekeeper-reported. The auditor counted this edit twice in its own summary (once as a lawful legibility split, once under SHAPE_MONOTONY for the leading-attribution frame) and missed the scope loss both times.
missedFindings.proposedFix: Keep both facts inside the account using the pool's own complement pattern: 'Those who hold the way through say the bar coming down is heard at the far doors, and that not one of the doors opens.' Reverting to the WAS line also cures it.

missedFindings.was: At the tavern they say the turn comes round to the same backs and never as far as the next roof.
missedFindings.now: At the tavern the same backs say the turn comes round to them and never as far as the next roof.
missedFindings.why: The auditor graded this NOTE and called the disagreement 'intact and sharper'. It is neither. In the WAS line 'the same backs' sits INSIDE the reported claim, so the pool asserts only that the tavern says the turn falls on the same backs - which is precisely what FACE 5's elders deny when they say it 'comes round to everyone who can spare a back'. In the NOW line 'the same backs' is the grammatical subject of 'say' and therefore outside the report, where it is a definite noun phrase in the narrator's voice presupposing that an identifiable group of repeatedly-burdened households exists. A presupposition is not defeasible the way a reported opinion is. A game master reading the new line learns as engine fact the thing pair 1 exists to leave open, and the elders' half is refuted by the frame before it is read. That is the one thing a disagreement pair may not do, and it is not covered by the old refutation, which was run against a tavern assertion and not an engine-held fact. The auditor's separate observation that 'the same' now has no antecedent is correct but is the smaller half of the defect.
missedFindings.proposedFix: Keep the contested proposition inside the reported clause and take the 42d stake from the speaker's own back: 'At the tavern the drinkers say the turn comes round to their own backs and never as far as the next roof.' The auditor's fix ('the households that turn out say the turn comes round to them') cures the presupposition but leaves the first clause near-tautological, since households that turn out are by definition the ones the turn reaches, and the whole bite then rests on the trailing clause.

overturnedFindings.why: The finding does not survive, on the text of the rule it invokes. 42a states its own test: 'delete the SECOND sentence. If the first is now missing a FACT, the second earns its place.' Run it. Delete 'The people here ask them straight out to put a shoulder to a load' and the first sentence retains no fact about WHAT is wanted, so the second earns its place and the test returns PASS. The auditor inverted the test, deleted the FIRST sentence instead, and reported a breach. Neither 42 nor 42a as quoted reaches a leading abstraction: 42 strikes 'a second clause that only EXPLAINS the first', which is a rule about what follows, not what precedes. The finding also cannot land because its fix deletes an attributed claim. 'The place says plainly what it wants of them' and 'the people here ask them straight out' name different actors - the settlement as an institution, which this pool consistently calls 'the place' when it is acting as an authority (V2 FACE 7, 'the place takes from whoever can be found'), against its residents asking informally - so the auditor's ground that the first is merely 'the abstract version of the concrete sentence that follows' is not established, and 'nothing is lost' is false. Under the claim freeze a fix may no more delete a fact than a re-cut may. What is genuinely wrong at this face is the attribution the split dropped, which the auditor cleared; it is carried in the family finding above. If a chair still wants the leading abstraction gone, that is a drafting note for a seat that can re-refute, not a finding against this cut.

overturnedFindings.faceOrSpine: POOL (all three variants) - SHAPE_MONOTONY, as filed
overturnedFindings.why: The finding's only piece of instance evidence is false and it cannot land in this form. It states that V2 FACE 5 'converted the pool's only fact-first line' into leading attribution. Ten fact-first lines survive the cut: V1 F1 ('The bar at the way through is kept by the doors nearest it, those who hold the way say'), V1 F3, V1 F7, V1 F9, V2 F1, V2 F3, V2 F9, V3 F1, V3 F4 and V3 F7 - four of them inside the changed set, all still fact-first after the edit. Second, fact-first versus attribution-first is not one of the five lawful shapes the brief names (FOUND, DOES, two people DISAGREE, nobody HAS DONE, the bare fact the engine holds); both orderings are 'a role says a fact', so re-ordering within that shape neither adds nor subtracts one, and V2 FACE 5 did not 'make it worse by one'. The headline claim - that the cut introduced no new sentence shape - I do not dispute and did not test against, and it can be re-filed on its own; but a SHOULD_FIX resting on a count of one that is actually a count of ten must be corrected before a chair acts on it.

missedFindings.was: A pedlar says the next house along has the same fields and the same year as the first.
missedFindings.now: A travelling trader says he found the next house along with the same fields and the same year as the first.
missedFindings.why: The auditor filed this as a small evidential sharpening ("says he found" adds that the speaker was there himself) and stopped. The larger move is one of TENSE AND ASPECT, and it is the move the freeze exists to catch. "has the same fields and the same year" is a STANDING condition of that farm: it is true of the next house along, full stop. "he found ... with the same fields and the same year" is ONE VISIT ON ONE OCCASION. A game master reading the new line believes a particular trader saw this once on his way in; the old line licensed the far stronger thing, that this is how the neighbouring land stands. That is a licence the new line DROPS, and it is load-bearing here: this face is half of disagree pair 1, and it only bites against the elders' standing claim ("the answer to a hungry year here is the next house along") if the next house's condition is standing too. One trader's one look does not refute a standing arrangement. The chair's own recorded read of this batch names exactly this class - C3, "42d's cure tempts a habitual present into a single past episode" - and lists two instances (granary AND hospital v3 f7, granary AND parish care only v2 f7). This pool's V1 FACE 2 is an unlisted third instance, and the wave gate's new "C3 is this clause historical?" rows (three lines with no HEAD counterpart) are the mechanical footprint of the same class.
missedFindings.proposedFix: Keep the habitual and still put him in it, which is the chair's own cure for the class: "A travelling trader who came that way says the next house along has the same fields and the same year as the first."

missedFindings.was: A pedlar says the next house along has the same fields and the same year as the first.
missedFindings.now: A travelling trader says he found the next house along with the same fields and the same year as the first.
missedFindings.why: The re-cut MANUFACTURED a two-reading sentence where the old line had none, which is 42b run backwards. "found the next house along with the same fields" garden-paths on the collocation "along with": the reader can parse it as "found [the next house along] [with the same fields]" or as "found the next house [along with] the same fields", i.e. found the house together with the fields. The old "the next house along HAS the same fields" admitted only one reading because the verb blocked the collocation. 42b says if two readings fit the sentence it makes no claim; the cure for the finding above happens to cure this one too.
missedFindings.proposedFix: Restore the finite verb: "... says the next house along has the same fields and the same year as the first."

missedFindings.was: Those who sell at the market SAY the same sacks ... / At the parish they SAY the tithe is weighed ...
missedFindings.now: Those who sell at the market RECKON the same sacks ... / At the parish they HOLD THAT the tithe is weighed ...

They are in fact two instances of a class the programme has already remedied: the chair's recorded read of this same batch carries C8, "ADEQUATE and WEAK need plain non-gloss report verbs restored (the batches 1-3 remedy)", so gloss report verbs are a named, precedented defect and not a matter of taste. Both edits spend the only change made to an otherwise passing face on making the report verb worse. "reckon" demotes a market seller's report of where the sacks go into his guess about it, and the sellers are the people who would actually know; "hold that" promotes a parish procedural report into a maintained position, which implies a dispute the pool does not contain and is the weaker word for the most factual source tag in the pool. The same gloss verb appears elsewhere in the batch (granary AND hospital: "At the gate they reckon"), so this should be swept batch-wide, not fixed line by line.

Then sweep the batch for "reckon"/"hold that" introduced by this cut.

missedFindings.was: The tavern's own account is that the water is fetched from whichever source runs clean, and that what is not clean can be made so for a price.
missedFindings.now: At the tavern they say they fetch their water from whichever source runs clean. What is not clean can be made so for a price.
missedFindings.why: The auditor caught the scope break ("the water" -> "their water") and was right to call it BLOCKING, but named neither of the two things that produced it, so a chair reading the finding alone cannot see why the remedy takes the shape it does. First, the SPEAKER was substituted: "The tavern's own account" is the HOUSE's account of its own supply - the establishment speaking - and "At the tavern they say" is the COMPANY at the tables. The brief's freeze says in terms "DO NOT delete a speaker. DO NOT drop an attribution", and swapping the establishment for its patrons is that rule's business, not a stylistic choice; it is also precisely what tempted "their water", because the house plausibly owns a bucket and the drinkers do not. Second, the attribution was dropped from the split: "and that what is not clean can be made so for a price" was inside the tavern's account, and "What is not clean can be made so for a price." is now a bare narrator sentence. Ruling 40 permits the bare unattributed fact only where the ENGINE holds it; here it converts the pool's least reliable source's claim - that water treatment is a thing this town sells - into settlement truth. I do not raise the same charge against the other two splits in this pool (V1 FACE 4's and V2 FACE 5's second sentences), because the owner's own worked line carries the attribution across a split by adjacency ("A priest says the sick house takes anyone who comes. The grain store turns away anyone without an order."), and in those two the carry-over reading is the natural one. Here the opener was changed in the same edit, so the carry-over does not survive.
missedFindings.proposedFix: Restore both the house as speaker and the settlement scope: "The tavern's own account is that the water here is fetched from whichever source runs clean, and that what is not clean can be made so for a price." If the two-sentence shape is wanted, re-attribute the second: "... They say what is not clean can be made so for a price."

missedFindings.now: Proposed by the auditor: At the parish nobody weighs the tithe until the wheel has taken its share.
missedFindings.why: The audit's own shape remedy breaks the freeze it is auditing. The brief states "DO NOT delete a speaker. DO NOT drop an attribution", and the auditor's finding text says in its own words that the conversion should go "to a different lawful shape WITHOUT DELETING THE SPEAKER" - then proposes a line with no speaker in it. "At the parish" is a place, not a source: the parish's report that this is how the tithe is weighed becomes an unattributed statement that this is how it is weighed, which is the bare-fact shape ruling 40 licenses only where the engine holds the fact. Applied as written this would turn a [register] face into an engine assertion and would need fresh refutation. The shape complaint itself is sound and I sustain it; the remedy is not, and it should not be carried into the pool unexamined.

missedFindings.was: Among the elders the account is that the strips are laid out so that no house is favoured ...
missedFindings.now: The elders say the strips are laid out so that no house is favoured ...
missedFindings.why: The auditor collected ONE of the three opener conversions for re-refutation (V3 FACE 5, "the talk is" -> "the stallholders say") on the ground that it specifies who holds the claim where the old line left it floating. The same ground applies here and it was not collected. "Among the elders the account is that X" reports an account CURRENT AMONG the elders, which is compatible with some of them not holding it and with none of them having said it to anyone; "The elders say X" commits the elders as a body to asserting it. That firms who is on the hook for the claim, which is the thing a refuter checks against the card, and it is the same firming the gate reads as a new provenance citation. Either it is collected onto the 42b list with the other two, or it lands unrefuted.
missedFindings.proposedFix: Add to the 42b collection list: old "Among the elders the account is that ..." -> new "The elders say ...", reading chosen: the elders assert it as a body rather than it merely circulating among them. If the chair takes the A13 fix above, collect that wording instead, since it changes the speaker again.

overturnedFindings.faceOrSpine: VARIANT 3 FACE 1 [elders] - the auditor's RULING_42_BREACH, "cut the clause the therefore was flagging"
overturnedFindings.why: The clause carries an independent fact, so 42a's own test keeps it, and the auditor's remedy would itself break the freeze. The auditor's argument is that "if no house is favoured in the layout of the strips, then a short year being short for every house follows with no new fact added". It does not follow. The first clause is about ALLOCATION - how the strips were laid out. The second is about EXPOSURE - what happens to every house when the year is short. The step from one to the other needs the further premise that no house has anything laid by to cushion it, and that premise is the POOL'S STATE (NO reserves), not anything the sentence says. A game master given only "the strips are laid out so that no house is favoured" can perfectly well picture houses that ride out a short year on something other than their strips; the second clause is what closes that off. Apply 42a as written - delete the second clause and ask whether the first is now missing a FACT - and the answer is yes, so it earns its place. The auditor's proposed fix ("The elders say the strips are laid out so that no house is favoured.") therefore DROPS a claim the old line licensed, which is the precise failure the claim freeze exists to prevent and is worse than the defect it is aimed at. The implementer's actual edit - deleting "therefore" and leaving two coordinate facts - is the correct 42 cure: "therefore" was the writer drawing the inference for the reader, and removing the signpost while keeping the fact is what 42 asks for. The chair's own read of this batch, recorded before any auditor returned, lands in the same place independently: its C2 fix for this line rewrites the opener and explicitly notes "(measured PRESENT; the 42 cut of `therefore` is kept)", retaining the clause the auditor wants gone.

overturnedFindings.faceOrSpine: VARIANT 3 FACE 2 [register] - the rule cited, RULING_42c_ARCHAISM_LEFT
overturnedFindings.why: The rule does not apply; nothing archaic is present or left in this face. 42c withdraws the archaism licence and names replacements for specific struck words (granary, infirmary, pedlar, factor, watchman, sexton, alehouse, bier, billhook, gaol, night patrolman). "hold that" is on none of those lists, is not an archaism, and 42c is not a rule about report verbs at all - the auditor's own reasoning for the finding ("the less plain of the two", "duplicates the construction already used") is a plainness-and-churn argument wearing a 42c label. The substance of the complaint survives and I have re-filed it, at higher severity, under the standing batches 1-3 remedy for gloss report verbs, which is the rule that actually governs it. Labelling matters here because the chair triages by rule: a 42c row implies an unstruck archaism is still sitting in the pool, and none is.

result.summary:
THE AUDIT'S SPINE HOLDS AND ITS TWO BLOCKING CALLS ARE RIGHT, but it missed a moved claim, missed a gate row this pool's cut newly raises, under-rated two edits that breach a standing remedy, left two sharpenings uncollected, and proposed one remedy that would itself break the freeze.

VERIFIED FIRST. The header counts are accurate (10 changed + 5 unchanged = 15 faces, 3 spines, 18 lines; I counted the CHANGED tags myself). The pools2 copy of this file is byte-identical to the audited one, so the audit is not against a stale cut. No mechanical bar is breached in any new line - no em dash, exclamation, digit, semicolon, contraction, first person, "will"/"shall", loose {settlement}, or bare singular role. Both disagreement pairs still genuinely disagree. And the audit's process finding is CONFIRMED by reading the brief: kit/briefs/brief-block-clarity-recut.md carries 42, 42a, 42b, 42c and the shape rule and contains NO 42d and no stake language, so the implementer cut ~550 faces without the speaker's-stake test. That finding is the most valuable thing in the return and should be acted on before the next batch.

THE MISSED MOVED CLAIM is VARIANT 1 FACE 2. The auditor caught the evidential half ("says he found" adds that he was there) and filed it NOTE. The half it missed is aspect: "the next house along HAS the same fields and the same year" is a standing condition of that land; "he FOUND the next house along with the same fields" is one visit on one occasion. The old line licensed a standing state, the new one licenses only an episode, and the disagree pair depends on the standing reading - one trader's one look does not answer the elders' standing claim that the next house along is the answer to a hungry year. This is an unlisted third instance of a class the chair already named in this batch (C3, "42d's cure tempts a habitual present into a single past episode"), and the wave gate's three new "is this clause historical?" rows are its footprint. The same edit also manufactures a two-reading sentence out of a one-reading one, because "found the next house along with the same fields" garden-paths on "along with".

THE MISSED GATE ROW is VARIANT 3 FACE 1. The chair's recorded instrument run reports a new A13 "a cited holder the census does not license", SOURCE-UNRESOLVED, on this pool alone, provenance 0 citations / 0 rows going to 1 / 1, caused by "The elders say" reading as provenance to the move classifier where the old impersonal opener did not. An audit of the prose alone could not see it; it is nonetheless a defect in this pool and it is not a taste matter.

WHAT I OVERTURN. The RULING_42_BREACH on VARIANT 3 FACE 1 does not survive. "A short year is short for every house" is not entailed by "the strips are laid out so that no house is favoured" - the first is about allocation, the second about exposure, and the step between them needs the premise that nothing is laid by, which is the pool's state and not in the sentence. 42a's own test therefore keeps the clause, and the auditor's fix would delete a licensed claim, which is a worse freeze breach than the one it is aimed at. Deleting "therefore" while keeping the fact is the correct 42 cure, and the chair's independently recorded fix for this line keeps the clause and keeps the "therefore" cut. I also overturn the RULE cited on VARIANT 3 FACE 2: nothing archaic is present, 42c names struck words and not report verbs, and the real rule is the batches 1-3 remedy for gloss report verbs - under which that edit and the "reckon" edit are precedented defects rather than churn.

THE UNSAFE REMEDY. The auditor's fix for its own shape finding - "At the parish nobody weighs the tithe until the wheel has taken its share" - deletes the speaker from an attributed [register] face, which the brief forbids in terms and which the auditor's own finding text says not to do. If applied it turns a sourced report into an engine assertion needing fresh refutation. The shape complaint itself is sound and I sustain it; the remedy must not be carried across. The shape finding also miscounts internally - it says only two faces use another lawful shape and then names three - but the substance (12 or 13 of 15 faces are now a role-asserts-a-fact frame, and the cut converted three non-asserting openers into asserting ones) holds either way. Note for the chair that the brief asks for shape variation to be judged ACROSS the batch of six, not within one pool.

THE AUDITOR'S THREE LEAST-SURE LINES, RESOLVED. (1) "reckon": the auditor should have gone further, not less far - it is a gloss report verb against a standing batches 1-3 remedy, not a matter of taste. (2) "he found": not lawful stake-work inside the freeze - it is the chair's own C3 class and the claim moves in aspect, as above. (3) "everybody at the table": the auditor's BLOCKING call is SUSTAINED. "here" means the town everywhere else in this pool ("a hungry year here", "Asked here what is done", "nobody here buys", and the V2 spine's "Everyone here knows"), and the chair independently ruled the identical narrowing a moved claim in another pool of this same batch ("nobody here" to "no drinker there" - "nobody here is the town; no drinker there is the tavern. The claim narrowed"). One calibration note: the chair rates that identical class SHOULD_FIX where the auditor rates it BLOCKING.

WHAT I CONSIDERED AND DECLINED TO RAISE. I do not charge the other two sentence splits (V1 FACE 4's and V2 FACE 5's second sentences) with dropping an attribution, even though each now stands unattributed, because the owner's own worked line carries attribution across a split by adjacency and 42a says two sentences are fine. I raise it only on V2 FACE 4, where the opener was changed in the same edit so the carry-over does not survive. I also note without charging it that the chair's gate run shows WITHHELDs rising on six pools from exactly these splits ("a second sentence naming no second field"), an accepted cost declared in batches 1-3, so the auditor's praise of the splits is fair but incomplete - they are not free.

BOTTOM LINE. The cut is real work and mostly good work; both archaisms are gone and the worst explaining clauses are broken up. But it is not landable as audited. Before it lands: fix V2 FACE 4 (speaker and scope), V1 FACE 4 ("here"), V1 FACE 2 (habitual), V3 FACE 1 (the A13 opener, keeping the clause), revert the two gloss verbs, cut V2 FACE 2's disclaimer clause entirely, collect four sharpenings rather than two, and discard the shape remedy as proposed.
